The vocabulary of the [Cache](/en/documentation/build/cache/) documentation, one row per term, each linked to the page that owns it.

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Bypass Cache | The [Rules Engine](/en/documentation/platform/applications/rules-engine/#bypass-cache) behavior that sends every request its rule matches to the origin and caches nothing. It runs in the **Request Phase**, requires [Application Accelerator](/en/documentation/build/application-accelerator/), and has the API type `bypass_cache`. It does not change the browser cache, which **Set Cache Policy** governs. |
| cache key | The index entry under which Cache stores an object. The default key concatenates the scheme, host, path, and query string of the request, and every variation is appended after the `@@` separator. Keys are case sensitive, and [Cache keys](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-keys/) documents the format with every variation it can carry. |
| cache key purge | The [Real-Time Purge](/en/documentation/build/cache/real-time-purge/) type that removes the objects a list of cache keys names, `cachekey` in the API. A key can name a variation by query string, cookie, or image format, and a purge of every variation lists each key. It is the one purge type the [Tiered Cache](/en/documentation/build/cache/tiered-cache/) layer accepts. |
| cache setting | The object, created on the **Cache Settings** tab of an application, that holds the TTLs and the variation rules Cache applies to a request. Its fields cover the browser cache, the cache behavior and **Max Age**, **Stale cache**, **Large file optimization**, **Tiered Cache**, and the four **Cache vary by** controls. A cache setting applies to no request until a **Set Cache Policy** rule names it, and [Cache settings](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-settings/) documents every field. |
| cache status | The status of a response in Cache, which the `x-cache` debug header reports. The values are `HIT`, `MISS`, `EXPIRED`, `STALE`, `UPDATING`, `REVALIDATED`, and `BYPASS`, and a response the platform does not cache reports `-`. [Cache keys](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-keys/) defines each value. |
| cache variation | A copy of an object that Cache stores under its own key because a query string argument, a cookie, a device group, the request method, an image format, or a byte range of a large file differs. The Console groups the four **Cache vary by** controls, which vary the key by method, query string, cookie, and device group, under **Application Accelerator** on a cache setting, and [Application Accelerator settings](/en/documentation/build/application-accelerator/settings/) documents them. Variation by query string and cookie is also named Advanced Cache Key. |
| Large File Optimization | The Cache feature, turned on per cache setting with the **Large file optimization** toggle, that stores a large object as 1,024 kB fragments. Azion caches each fragment at the moment a user requests it, under its own cache key with a `@@bytes=` suffix. It applies to Cache and to Tiered Cache when that layer is on, and [How Cache works](/en/documentation/build/cache/how-it-works/) describes the mechanism. |
| Max Age | The Console field for the cache TTL: the seconds Cache keeps a copy of an object, `modules.cache.max_age` in the API. The default is `60` in the Console, the API, and the CLI. A value below 60 requires Application Accelerator on the application, Tiered Cache requires at least 3 seconds, and [Cache settings](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-settings/) documents the bounds. |
| Real-Time Purge | The platform resource that removes cached objects from Cache or Tiered Cache before their TTL ends, so the next request fetches the latest version from the origin. A purge names its objects by URL, by cache key, or by a wildcard expression, and Azion queues it after the confirmation message and lists it in the history when it completes. [Real-Time Purge](/en/documentation/build/cache/real-time-purge/) documents the three types and the layers each reaches. |
| Set Cache Policy | The [Rules Engine](/en/documentation/platform/applications/rules-engine/#set-cache-policy) behavior that names a cache setting and puts it in effect for the requests its rule matches. It runs in the **Request Phase**, its argument is the id of the cache setting, and the API type is `set_cache_policy`. A cache setting that no **Set Cache Policy** rule names applies to no request. |
| stale cache | The Cache behavior, turned on per cache setting with the **Stale cache** toggle, that serves an expired copy during a stale window when revalidation with the origin fails. Under _Honor cache policies_ the window is the origin's `stale-while-revalidate` value, and under _Override cache behavior_, or when the origin omits the directive, it is 300 seconds. During the window Azion fetches a fresh version in the background, and [How Cache works](/en/documentation/build/cache/how-it-works/) lists what counts as a failed revalidation. |
| Tiered Cache | The second cache layer that sits between Azion's cache and the origin, turned on per cache setting with the **Tiered Cache** toggle and included in every plan. It keeps objects longer and in a region chosen by its topology, and it requires _Override cache behavior_ and a **Max Age** of at least 3 seconds on the setting. [Tiered Cache](/en/documentation/build/cache/tiered-cache/) documents the layer, its topologies, and how a purge reaches it. |
| topology | The Tiered Cache setting that selects the region where the second cache layer holds objects. It takes `nearest-region`, `br-east-1`, or `us-east-1`, in the API field `modules.cache.tiered_cache.topology`. [Tiered Cache](/en/documentation/build/cache/tiered-cache/) documents the layer it configures. |
| TTL | The number of seconds Cache or the browser keeps a copy of an object, set per [cache setting](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-settings/) by **Max Age** for Azion's cache and by `browser_cache.max_age` for the browser. |
| URL purge | The [Real-Time Purge](/en/documentation/build/cache/real-time-purge/) type that removes the object each URL in a list names, `url` in the API. It is not recursive, and Azion converts each URL to its cache key without the variations, so a variation by cookie, device group, or image format needs a cache key or wildcard purge. A URL without a scheme purges both the HTTP and the HTTPS object. |
| wildcard purge | The [Real-Time Purge](/en/documentation/build/cache/real-time-purge/) type, `wildcard` in the API, that removes every object one expression with `*` in the path or the query string matches. An expression can carry more than one `*`, and a request carries one expression. It is not available for the Tiered Cache layer. |
| `x-cache` | The debug response header that carries the cache status of a response, the IP of the server that answered, and the protocol. Azion returns it when the request carries the header `Pragma: azion-debug-cache`. [Cache keys](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-keys/) lists every status value it can carry. |
| `x-cache-key` | The debug response header that carries the cache key of the response. Azion returns it when the request carries the header `Pragma: azion-debug-cache`, and a response the platform does not cache carries `x-cache-key: -`. [Cache keys](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-keys/) documents the format of the key. |
